title: Introduce lightweight retrieval-agent playground with step-debugger
author: Priya Patel
release_notes: Adds a minimal, local-first retrieval-agent playground with a turn-based step debugger and authoring hints; useful for prototyping tool-calling flows and teaching prompt-authoring best practices.
description:
Context: Engineers and SDK users frequently ask for a small, self-contained sandbox to iterate on retrieval-augmented agents and tool-calling logic without standing up the full infra. This PR introduces a lightweight 'Retrieval Agent Playground' (RAP) that runs locally, demonstrates retrieval+tools, and — importantly — provides a deterministic turn-based step debugger to inspect internal agent decisions (tool selection, calls, and retrieval traces).

What this changes: adds an examples/playground that focuses on developer feedback loops rather than production-scaled infra. The playground includes: a tiny express-based dev server, an embeddable UI for replaying agent steps, a mock vector index (file-backed) with seeded fixtures, sample tool adapters (search, calculator, web-mock), and a step-debugger that records each agent decision and exposes a route for replaying and stepping through state. Also adds docs and a quickstart README with troubleshooting and suggested prompt templates.

Why: reduces onboarding time for new users who want to test RAG/tool-calling flows, helps PMs and engineers reproduce edge-cases from logs, and provides a reproducible environment for evaluation harnesses. The step-debugger was intentionally implemented as a dev-only hook that serializes KV cache state and tool call transcripts to JSON; production runtimes are unaffected.

How to run (summary): 1) cd examples/retrieval-agent-playground 2) npm ci && npm run seed && npm start 3) open http://localhost:4000/playground to author prompts and http://localhost:4000/debug/trace/:traceId to step through decisions. The README contains request examples to exercise streaming/structured outputs and tool fallbacks.

Checklist: - [x] Playground server and seed script added - [x] Example prompt sets (happy and failure paths) - [x] Step debugger UI + API route - [x] Basic telemetry hooks (dev-only) - [x] Quickstart docs and troubleshooting - [x] CI smoke test to boot server in container

Security and privacy: The playground stores fixtures locally and is flagged as dev-only in the README. No telemetry is shipped to external services by default. Keys and production endpoints are not included.

Testing and CI: Added a lightweight integration job that boots the playground in CI container and runs smoke requests against the primary routes. The first CI run failed due to a race condition in the seed script; fixed by adding a readiness probe and re-run succeeded. CI summary is included below.

Related work: follows patterns from ENG-4821 to make interactive debugging available for agent flows; complements the eval harness examples and local authoring tooling in the docs site.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the step debugger serialization format (examples/playground/src/debug/serializer.ts) which is intentionally compact; we plan to extend this for recorded-evals but kept the first pass small.

Merge notes: Squash-merged to keep commit history focused. No release gating required for mainline.

notes_for_backport_or_followup: Follow-up tasks: 1) ENG-4821 follow-up to add recorded-eval upload path and opt-in flag; 2) add typescript typings for trace schema and expose a small SDK helper; 3) consider a separate repo template for customers wanting a hosted dev-sandbox.
manual_qa_steps: 1) Run seed and start local server. 2) Use playground UI to issue a tool-heavy prompt that triggers fallback logic. 3) Note traceId returned in response and open /debug/trace/:traceId. 4) Step through decisions and confirm tool call arguments, retrieved passages, and KV cache snapshots. 5) Run npm run smoke-ci locally to validate the readiness probe behavior.
